newsitem.title: USA: Storm kills power to 160,000 New England customers.
newsitem.headline: Storm kills power to 160,000 New England customers.

text.p: A furious storm that dumped up to a foot of heavy wet snow in parts of New England left more than 160,000 homes without power on Sunday, officials said.

"MassElectric reports that they have about 120,000 customers without power, Boston Edison says they have 20,000 and in the western part of the state there are another 20,000," said Jerry Meister, director of operations for the Massachusetts Emergency Management Agency.
He said that while Boston Edison expected to restore service to its customers by the end of the day, it would be late Monday or Tuesday before MassElectric's customers would be fully restored.
Emergency crews from New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island were brought in to help restore power, he said.

Todd McLeish, a spokesman for Blackstone Valley Electric, the subsidiary of Eastern Utilities Associates that serves Rhode Island, said 7,000 customers in the northern part of the state lost power on Saturday night. By midday Sunday all but 500 customers had power.
New Hampshire was also hard hit. Officials at that state's emergency agency said they were still trying to get a handle on the scope of the problem and readying shelters.
Likewise the Massachusetts Red Cross was preparing to shelter thousands in the Merrimack Valley area whose homes were expected to remain without power.

In Connecticut, more than 100,000 were without power for many hours beginning late on Saturday due mainly to the heavy snow pulling down wires. Most were back on line by midday Sunday but as in other areas of the region, some were expected to be without power until Monday.
